history.recommendation_text: The Board recommended that the Administration make continuous efforts to trace the refunds outstanding of country-based pooled funds projects that were already paid by implementing partners, and coordinate with the Finance Division to record them in Umoja in a timely manner.
history.administration_response: To enhance internal control to regularly monitor, review, follow up on and record outstanding refunds that were already paid by implementing partners, the Administration has created a weekly status report to closely follow up on outstanding refunds with the Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs. Management will continue to work with partners and the Finance Division to trace the refunds. The Office notes that a one major reason for the difficulty in tracing refunds is the absence of a data transfer bridge between Umoja and the grant management system. It continues to follow up on the data transfer bridge, but emphasizes that its development is beyond its direct control.
history.board_assessment: Given that, although the Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs has been following up continuously on outstanding refunds with partners and working closely with finance to trace and record them, the data bridge between the grant management system and Umoja is still absent, which is the major reason for the difficulty in tracing refunds. The Board therefore considers this recommendation to be under implementation.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommended that the Administration make continuous efforts to trace the refunds outstanding of country- based pooled fund projects that were already paid by implementing partners and coordinate with the Finance Division to record them in Umoja in a timely manner.
history.administration_response: Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs: Such continuous efforts are reflected in the steady progress that continues to be made in addressing aged claims and refunds, although there will always be some pending refunds owing to the ongoing cycle of new grants and projects. The Country-Based Pooled Fund Section at Headquarters receives a weekly report on refund statistics from the Office of Programme Planning, Finance and Budget. A dedicated team has been assigned to ensure that pending incoming refunds, as well as the backlog of refunds from previous years, are being recorded in Umoja and updated in the One Grant Management System on a daily basis. For example, the materiality of these pending refunds has been considerably reduced, from $19 million to $6 million. Discussions on the bridge between the One Grant Management System and Umoja are ongoing with the Office of Programme Planning, Finance and Budget.
history.board_assessment: Given that the Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs receives a weekly report on refunds from the Office of Programme Planning, Finance and Budget and has made efforts to reduce the pending refunds from $19 million to $6 million, the Board considers the recommendation to be implemented.
